chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Yunus ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام), “This thing that has appeared on my face—people claim that Allah does not afflict a servant with it while He has a need of him.” He said to me, “Indeed, the believer from the family of Fir‘awn had contracted fingers, and he would gesture like this, stretching out his hands, and say:”

Then he said to me, “When the last third of the night begins, perform wudu (ablution) and stand for the salat (prayer) you pray. Then when you are in the final sajdah of the first two rak‘ahs, say while you are prostrating: ‘O Most High, O Most Great, O Most Beneficent, O Most Merciful, O Hearer of supplications, O Giver of good things, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and give me of the good of this world and the Hereafter that befits You, and turn away from me of the evil of this world and the Hereafter that befits You, and remove from me this pain’—and name it—‘for it has angered me and saddened me.’ And persist in the supplication.”
He said: “I had not reached al-Kufah before Allah had removed it from me entirely.”

key_terms.الثُّلُثُ الْأَخِيرُ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ: the last third of the night, a spiritually significant time for worship and supplication
key_terms.الدُّعَاءِ: supplication, in which one is instructed to be persistent
key_terms.السَّجْدَةِ الْأَخِيرَةِ: the final sajdah, the specific place in salat where the du'a is to be recited
key_terms.الْوَجَعِ: the pain or ailment for which relief is being sought
key_terms.صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad
key_terms.فَتَوَضَّ: perform wudu (ablution) before engaging in prayer and supplication
key_terms.مُؤْمِنُ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ: the believing man from the family of Fir‘awn, cited as an example of a righteous person afflicted physically
key_terms.يَا سَامِعَ الدَّعَوَاتِ: O Hearer of supplications, a divine invocation emphasizing Allah’s response to prayer

ai.seo_question: What du'a did Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) teach for relief from illness or bodily pain?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a complaint of physical affliction brought to Imam Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام), who rejects the idea that bodily trial indicates a lack of divine concern by citing the believing man from the family of Fir‘awn. The Imam (عليه السلام) then teaches a specific night supplication in sajdah, combining wudu (ablution), salat (prayer), invocation of divine names, salawat upon Muhammad and آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ, and persistence in du'a (supplication).

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Malik Bin Atiyya, from Yunus Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘This which has appeared in my face, the people are alleging that Allahazwj does not Afflict a servant with it in whom Heazwj has a need’. So heasws said to me: ‘It was so that the Momin from the people of the Paharohla was of a paralytic fingers, and he was speaking like this, and he was extending his hands and saying, ‘[36:20] O people! Follow the Rasools’.

Then heasws said to me: ‘When it is the last third of the night, during its beginning, so perform ablution and stand to your Salāt which you tend to pay. So when you are in the last Sajda from the first two Cycles, say while you are in the Sajda,

‘O Exalted! O Beneficent! O Merciful! O Hearer of the supplications! O Given of the goodness! Send Blessings upon Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, and Give me from the goodness of the world and the Hereafter what You<sup>azwj</sup> are Rightful of, and Exchange from me the evil of the world and the Hereafter what You<sup>azwj</sup> are Rightful of; and Remove this pain from me’, and name it, ‘For it has enrages me and grieved me’. And be insistent in the supplication’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So I had not arrived in Al-Kufa until Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> had Removed it from me, all of it’.
en.sarwar: 30. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Malik ibn ‘Atiyyah from Yunus ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“Once I said to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘About this thing that has appeared on my face, people think Allah does not make suffer (from this) any servant in whom He is interested.’ The Imam said, ‘The believer among the people of Pharaoh had crippled fingers. He would extend his fingers and say, “My people follow the Messengers (of Allah).’

Then the Imam said to me, ‘In the beginning of the third part of the night get up and make Wuzu and stand up for your prayer that you pray. In the last prostration of first two Rak’at say, “O the Most high, the Most great, O Beneficent, O Merciful, O the One Who listens to the prayers, O the One Who grants all good, bestow blessings upon Muhammad and his family, recipients of divine supreme covenant, and grant me the good things of the world and of the next life and of that which You deem proper to grant me. Remove from me the evil of this world and of the hereafter and of that which You deem proper to grant and remove from me this pain - mention its name - it has angered and depressed me,” Then insist pleading. ’
The narrator has said that before I reached al-Kufah, Allah had removed that entire thing from my face.”
